_note: Laws of Pangu — tunables shared by every world, not per-world settings.
A world config opts in with a top-level "laws": "laws.json" key; the file is
resolved beside that config, never against the working directory.
Blocks a config declares itself are merged OVER these, so a world can override a
law — but only deliberately, and only with the reason written into that config
(see configs/fire_arena.json). Test: would making this evolvable let organisms
escape a constraint the simulation exists to impose? If yes, it belongs here — AD-13.
_chi_note: Both chi values are LAWS by AD-13's test: an evolvable deficit threshold would be
driven to its ceiling and an evolvable conversion rate with it, which together
abolish Water starvation — the exact pressure the legs organ system exists to
impose. Read by ChiPool (chi.py), the single conversion site.
DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN — Story 1.2, 2026-08-12. Regenerate every table below with
python tools/derive_chi_laws.py all
which sweeps workshop mode over 12 seeds x 6000 ticks per grid point, with each of
the four archetypes pinned in turn — a threshold expressed as a fraction of capacity
buys a different absolute buffer to the specialist (Water capacity 10) than to the
hoarder (40), so sweeping only the archetype the workshop happens to spawn would
derive a number that is wrong for half the population.
THE METRIC. `preventable` is leg integrity lost on ticks where the bot still held
at least 1.0 Metal — starvation a conversion law could have prevented and did not.
Total integrity loss cannot derive anything here: it is dominated by bots dying with
every pool empty, which no conversion reaches, and is nearly flat across the whole
grid (38-42 in the workshop at every setting tried). Splitting the preventable part
out is what turns that plateau into a knee.
deficit_conversion_rate = 0.025.
Holding the threshold at 0.03 and sweeping the rate, preventable loss for the
0.016 and stays at 0.00 above that. The worst archetype (hoarder) is slower to clear:
0.53 at 0.020, 0.10 at 0.025, 0.06 at 0.032. So the measured knee is around 0.016 and
the chosen value sits above it, deliberately — margin on the safe side, not the
cheapest value that works.
A mechanical prediction lands in the same octave: the demand path has to replace a
whole tick's leg draw out of whatever Metal is left, so
rate >= drain_max / (CYCLE_EFFICIENCY x metal floor) = 0.020 / (0.8 x 1.0) = 0.025.
TREAT THAT AS A SANITY CHECK, NOT A SECOND MEASUREMENT. It shares the 1.0 Metal
floor with the metric above, so the two are not independent, and
`derive_chi_laws.py floor` shows how much that matters: at a metric floor of 0.25
(predicted rate 0.100) the measured knee moves out to 0.064, and at 4.0 (predicted
0.0062) it stays at 0.016 rather than following. The knee's *shape* — a collapse
over roughly one octave of rate, in the same place for every archetype and under
contention as well as in the workshop — is the real evidence. Its third significant
figure is not.
water_deficit_threshold = 0.008.
Held at rate 0.025, worst-archetype preventable loss is 14.55 at 0.001, 1.07 at
0.060, 0.120. It collapses by two orders of magnitude before 0.008 and is flat
after. The flat values are NOT ordered — 0.120 reads marginally lower than 0.008 —
and that ordering is noise, not a reason to prefer a larger threshold: the per-seed
spread within each of those cells (0.045-0.052, printed as the `spread` column) is
as large as the differences between them, and a single seed contributes essentially
the whole total. What is NOT noise is the cost, which rises monotonically the whole
way: Metal converted by the demand path, default archetype, goes 132 -> 135 -> 156
threshold that buys all of the prevention that is available to buy.
Mechanically it is four ticks of the fastest leg draw held in the smallest Water
pool in play: 4 x 0.020 / 10.0 (specialist capacity) = 0.008. Four rather than one
because the chi phase runs after upkeep, so the trigger is always reacting to the
tick before — see the residual note below.
WHY A LARGER THRESHOLD BUYS NOTHING. The demand path is a REGULATOR, not a pulse: it
asks for the shortfall, so it restores Water to the threshold and no further. The
pool is topped up every tick either way; the threshold sets how much sits in it, not
how often the path runs. That is also why the two constants could be derived against
separate criteria at all.
RESIDUAL. ~0.1 of preventable loss survives at every setting. That is the first tick
of a deficit, which no threshold reaches, because the chi phase runs AFTER upkeep —
the legs drain and degrade before conversion is consulted. Raising the threshold
fifteenfold does not reduce it, which is what identifies it as the ordering rather
than the buffer. AD-1 puts chi before upkeep and would remove it; reordering was
deferred with its own baseline (see deferred-work.md) because it changes behaviour
above the threshold, and `test_the_tick_runs_the_phases_in_the_recorded_order` pins
the order being held in the meantime.
AD-14 TRANSFER CHECK — `derive_chi_laws.py transfer`, default_world, 12 seeds x 4000
ticks, 20 bots with archetypes cycled as shipped, resources per bot 7.5 against the
workshop's 23. Preventable loss 401.1 (+-34.7) with the path off -> 0.32 (+-0.10) at
the derived pair: 99.9% removed. Total leg integrity loss 616.8 -> 503.9. Mean Metal
9.87 -> 9.16, so Metal remains the healthiest pool, which is why it is the donor. The
knees sit in the same places under contention: rate 0.012 still leaves 8.66
preventable and 0.020 leaves 0.45, while thresholds from 0.004 to 0.060 are all
within each other's spread (0.32-0.59) and only the Metal bill moves (1739 -> 2318).
_repair_note: Earth-funded structural repair (STR-2, AD-8). Laws by AD-13's test: an evolvable
exchange rate is driven to zero and damage becomes free; an evolvable floor is
driven to zero and a lineage heals its legs while the body starves. `mass` is the
trait that varies per part; these are the shared knobs.
DERIVED LOOSELY, ON PURPOSE — Story 1.3, 2026-08-17. Brad's direction: the goal is
working systems with enough resolution to see behaviour change, not a balanced
world. Real balance waits until bots are evolvable and can be selected rather than
tuned. So each value below is anchored to a stated mechanical quantity rather than
fitted to an outcome, and the sweep that checks them is a sanity check, not a
search. Re-derive against the full loop once selection exists —
tools/derive_repair_laws.py regenerates the checks.
max_integrity_per_tick = 0.002. THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. Without a per-tick cap a part
asks for its whole deficit at once and rebuilds the instant Earth allows: measured
before this law existed, legs never left 1.0000 across a 1200-tick run in which
repair fired continuously, so neither the dip nor the recovery was ever visible.
Anchored to the degrade rate: a leg starved at cruise loses ~0.005/tick, so repair
at 0.002 runs at roughly 2/5 of the damage rate. Starvation therefore outpaces
healing while it lasts (damage accumulates, as it should) and unwinds over a few
hundred ticks once fed. A full 0 -> 1 rebuild takes 500 ticks, the same order as the
longest measured dry spell (466).
earth_per_integrity_mass = 4.0. Anchored to the placeholder mass table, where every
organ system totals mass 4.0 by construction (Brad's rule that each system costs
about the same to repair). Fully rebuilding one whole system therefore costs
4.0 x 4.0 = 16 Earth against a storage capacity of 20 — most of a full pool, so
repair is a real economic choice rather than a rounding error, and still affordable
for a bot that is feeding. Per tick while repairing two legs: 2 x 0.002 x 1.0 x 4.0
= 0.016 Earth, against the Earth organ's own upkeep of 0.004-0.008 — repair roughly
triples Earth demand while it runs, which is the cost being visible.
earth_repair_floor = 2.0. Earth held back from repair so healing cannot starve the
one organ that kills (AD-6). At the Earth organ's 0.004-0.008/tick upkeep, 2.0
leaves 250-500 ticks of runway. The floor is load-bearing because _repair_parts
runs before _metabolize: without it a bot would spend its last Earth on legs and
then fail to fund the body on the same tick.
